checks.result: passed; stable fallback because nightly is unavailable

every individual assertion confirmed passing via a combination of full scenario runs and targeted manual step-by-step verification against real containers/kernel; the test environment repeatedly killed long-running automated Docker runs for memory pressure unrelated to this code before a single uninterrupted end-to-end run completed

docker_scenario.topology: 1 server + peer-a + peer-b on an isolated internal bridge, require-management network, real production build (reuses M2's topology)
docker_scenario.peer_a_happy_path: stage-management-rotation (server) -> stage-management (client, importing the transferred artifact) -> apply-management-rotation + apply-management (both sides) -> real fresh handshake and authenticated request succeed with matching PSKs confirmed on both sides -> mark-management-verified -> confirm-management-rotation + confirm-management -> a server+peer-a restart together, confirming the rotated (not original) PSK survives and the link still works
docker_scenario.peer_b_failure_and_repair_path: stage+apply only on the server (peer-b's client never touched) creates a real one-sided PSK mismatch; the link breaks (peer-b's own daemon logs 'Could not connect to the innernet server, proceeding with cached state instead', not a crash or a hang); rollback-management-rotation on the server alone repairs it out of band, restoring both the original PSK and reachability, since peer-b never left its original secret
docker_scenario.real_kernel_finding: wg set-ing a new PSK onto an already-established peer entry never tears down the existing session (WireGuard mixes the PSK into the *next* handshake only), so a rotation's apply step was silently leaving traffic encrypted under the superseded secret for up to REJECT_AFTER_TIME (~180s). Fixed in both client-core::management::push_active_to_kernel and server::push_management_psk_to_kernel by removing the peer (reading back its existing endpoint/allowed-ips/keepalive first, since removal drops them) and re-adding it whole -- design 5.10 step 2's 'remove old sessions'. Also found and fixed a test-script bug: wg show dump rows must be matched by public key, not endpoint, since a remove-then-re-add resets the observed endpoint to (none) until a fresh handshake arrives

limitations: automatic/mailbox-driven rotation is out of scope for v1 per design 5.10; every rotation primitive requires --independent-admin-access
no old/new binary compatibility requirement, consistent with M6's scope decision; no legacy-binary rotation interop was tested

the Docker scenario's every assertion was independently confirmed passing, but not captured in a single uninterrupted automated run, due to the test environment's memory-pressure interruptions during this milestone's work
